Osteocalcin: Table 1 prints mg/dL with values 116.5 (Month 4) and 47.2 (Month 39), whereas text gives 116.6 ng/mL and 47.2 ng/mL; Month 10 and Month 13 both print 254.

Values near the four-month presentation differ between text and Table 1: PTH 95 (text) vs 94 (Table 1); BALP 105 (text) vs 106 (Table 1); osteocalcin 116.6 ng/mL vs 116.5 mg/dL; crosslaps 4082 vs 4.082. Scintigraphy sites: b00016 lists focal uptake near the lateral wall of the 4th right rib, right elbow, left wrist, bilateral knees and ankles; b00061 reports a focal area near the right fourth rib with no other significant areas suggestive of multifocal lesions or Paget disease.

Follow-up timing is internally inconsistent: presentation at approximately four months, then "One month later (six months post-transplant)"; 25(OH)D 42 ng/mL reported at nine months in text but at Month 8 in Table 1 (Month 10 is 40); the first DEXA appears in the presentation work-up before cholecalciferol in the narrative but is labelled Month 6 in Table 2; abstract gives lumbar T-score −2.6 at 26 months while Table 2 gives −2.8 at Month 25 and the post-bisphosphonate DEXA also gives −2.6. The b00024/b00034 values (no own time) equal the Table 1/2 Month 39 cells.

Bisphosphonate timing: abstract lists oral bisphosphonate therapy within the regimen preceding recovery of independent ambulation within 9 months; b00022 says treatment was not begun after the nine-month visit; b00045 records agreement to start at a later evaluation; Fig. 5 places a "Start biphoshonates" marker between the Month 17 and Month 39 positions.

Recovery wording: abstract says independent ambulation was recovered within 9 months; body text says at nine months she walked independently with the aid of crutches and was fully independent without assistive devices only at 26 months.
Figure 2: caption and b00018 say X-rays of the shoulders and right knee, while the same paragraph describes Looser zones on the hip X-ray (Fig. 2); the image pixels show a pelvis radiograph.
Figure 5 unit labels: panel C is titled phosphate (mg/mL) with reference range 2.5-4.5 mg/mL whereas text and Table 1 use mg/dL; panel A title says ng/mL with a ng/dL reference label.
Hypophosphatemia is stated for phosphate 2.8 mg/dL although the Table 1 reference range is 2.5-4.5 mg/dL.

Osteomalacia certainty: initially "suspected", later "confirmed by imaging and bone turnover markers" and "supported ... as a major contributor"; bone biopsy was not performed; the authors also attribute disease to superimposed persistent hyperparathyroidism.

Mechanisms are postulated, not measured: probable excess FGF23 (FGF23 not measured), subclinical osteomalacia before transplantation, reduced sun exposure, steroid therapy and discontinuation of vitamin D supplementation as unmasking factors; vitamin D suspension timing and dose are not given.

Initial knee MRI laterality: b00018 states MRI of the left knee; abstract states bone-marrow edema of both knees; b00059 ends with "and bilateral"; bilateral knee MRI is documented at six and nine months.
One-year post-bisphosphonate osteocalcin (62.5 ng/mL) is higher than the earlier 47.2 although the text says markers showed further improvement; BALP 25 vs 24.8.

Naming differences: vertebrae D6/D7 (b00017) vs T6/T7 (b00045); DEXA site "total femur" in text vs "Total hip" in Table 2; "femoral" in text vs "Femoral neck" in Table 2; analyte "CTX" in text vs "Cross-laps" in Table 1; b00061 mentions absence of specific radiological signs of metabolic bone disease despite earlier Looser zones.
Date information is partial: kidney transplantation "in 2020" and hemodialysis "beginning in 2020" for approximately eight months; CKD diagnosed in 1997; no full calendar dates anywhere.
Pre-transplant care was at a different nephrology center; the rationale for solitary parathyroidectomy is unknown.

claims.text: A 61-year-old woman with CKD from IgA nephropathy (diagnosed 1997) was treated with peritoneal dialysis for 70 months and then hemodialysis from 2020. During dialysis she developed secondary hyperparathyroidism refractory to cinacalcet, calcitriol and paricalcitol (PTH up to 690 pg/mL, phosphate 7.7 mg/dL, calcium 10 mg/dL, enlarged parathyroid glands). Two months before transplantation a selective right inferior parathyroidectomy showed parathyroid adenoma.
